title: PostgreSQL Connection Pool Exhaustion Triggering Cascading Public Portal 504 Timeouts

alert_evidence.message: Database connection pool exhausted on primary instance
Database storage I/O wait latency critical
High database query timeout percentage on shelter query endpoint
Web frontend gateway timeout 504 errors on public homepage

log_evidence.message: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections (max_connections=100 reached)
ConnectionPoolTimeoutException: Timeout waiting for idle connection from pool after 5000ms
HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout while proxying request to upstream emergency-data-service:8080

trace_evidence.failed_span_operation: SELECT * FROM evacuation_shelters WHERE active = true

system_inferences.correlation_summary: Incident INC-001 was grouped because alerts ALT-101 through ALT-108 occurred within the configured 180s temporal window and involve services connected through the service dependency topology graph. PostgreSQL Database was identified as the leading candidate root cause because its resource saturation indicators preceded downstream API Gateway and Web Frontend failures by 18 to 29 seconds.
symptoms_identified: Web Frontend client timeout alerts increased
Emergency Data Service query timeout rate elevated
Public evacuation zone endpoint returning 504 status

probable_root_cause_candidates.reasoning: Earliest failure timestamp (10:02:11Z), root dependency in topology path, accompanied by FATAL connection exhaustion log (LOG-101) and trace error span (TRC-2001).
Intermediate hop showing query timeouts, but timestamps (10:02:22Z) show failure commenced after database exhaustion.
Purely symptomatic reverse-proxy timeout breaches triggered by stalled upstream responses.
